subject: Dedicated capacity: top-up/throttle slab for autoscale & surge safety-net
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Blake <sara@nimhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 15:30:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity: top-up/throttle slab for autoscale & surge safety-net

Hi Sara —

Thanks again for the deep dive last week. Per our call, I put together a concise proposal for a Dedicated + autoscale (burst) add-on that aims to balance predictable monthly commits with a transient surge safety-net for unpredictable clinic batch jobs. Key points in the attached spreadsheet (nim-topup-throttle-pricing-v1.xlsx):

- Reserved commit: baseline GPU pool (8 x A100 equivalent) for 24/7 throughput guarantees.
- Top-up slab model: credit slabs (small/medium/large) that purchase ephemeral headroom in blocks (per-hour granularity).
- Throttle / surge governor: a short cooldown (default 30m) and a per-customer surge-rate cap to avoid sustained over-provisioning.
- Grace credits: a small monthly buffer to cover short warm-starts before top-up consumption kicks in.

Questions for you: 1) Does hourly slab granularity work with your batch windows? 2) Any constraints on maximum per-minute throughput during overnight syncs? 3) Are you looking to cap total monthly spend or to cap sustained vCPU/GPU utilization?

If this is aligned, we can map pricing bands and a provisional discount schedule (we've penciled in a 12% sticker discount for a 12‑month commit in the spreadsheet). Marissa and Karthik are looped for pricing and packaging. Rafael can weigh in on billing terms if needed.

I attached the XLSX and a one‑pager outline. Happy to schedule a 30m follow-up.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
grace_oconnor@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-1290

Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 09:04:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: top-up/throttle slab for autoscale & surge safety-net

Grace —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the clear spreadsheet. A few clarifying questions from our side before we line up procurement: 

1) Burst ceiling: for our nightly ETL windows we sometimes spike up to ~6x baseline for ~45–75 minutes. Will the slab model allow consecutive slab consumption during that window or is there a hard throttle that would reject extra requests beyond X TPS?

2) Cooldown semantics: your 30m default — does that prevent re-entry (i.e., you disallow new slabs for 30m after a burst) or just slow the rate of refill? We need predictable behavior to avoid failing jobs mid-run.

3) Billing alignment: can we cap the monthly top-up spend? Ideally procurement needs a spend ceiling and an alerting hook before we breach it.

Also, procurement wants the terms that relate to unused slab refunds and how partial-hour consumption is billed. Could you send a short paragraph we can forward to procurement that summarizes these points?

Thanks —
Sara
Head of Platform Ops | Nimbus Health
sara@nimhealth.com | +1 (917) 555-2044
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Blake <sara@nimhealth.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 11:18:05 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: top-up/throttle slab for autoscale & surge safety-net

Sara —

Thanks for the clear questions. Short answers here and pasted language you can share with procurement below. Grace / Karthik / Rafael — I added pricing guidance inline.

1) Burst ceiling:
- The slab model is consumption-based: if you have 2 consecutive slabs available we will not reject requests while slabs remain. We do enforce a configurable surge-rate cap (default 4x baseline sustained over 60m).
- For your 45–75m nightly spikes we recommend the "large" slab bucket which is sized for sustained 3–6x peaks; pricing is lower per-GPU-hour for larger slabs.

2) Cooldown semantics:
- Cooldown is a soft governor to prevent immediate re-surge. Default "30m cooldown" is measured from the end of a slab consumption window; during cooldown an additional slab can be requested but it will incur an "expedited top-up" premium (20%) unless you opt-out. This lets you decide between deterministic safety (hard block) vs. availability with premium.

3) Billing cap / guardrails:
- We can put a hard monthly top-up spend cap on the account that will prevent further slab issuance once hit. We also produce pre-threshold alerts (70/85/95%) and a billing webhook you can subscribe to.

Procurement-ready paragraph (pasteable):
"Redwood offers a top-up slab add-on to Dedicated capacity that provides ephemeral GPU headroom in hourly blocks. Slabs are consumed on demand and priced per-GPU-hour with volume discounts for larger slabs. Default behavior includes a 30-minute cooldown (soft governor) to reduce thrash; during cooldown expedited top-ups are available at a premium. Customers may elect a hard monthly top-up spend cap and receive automated threshold alerts. Unused slab time is not refunded but is available for consumption during the billing month; partial-hour consumption is pro-rated to the minute."

Pricing notes (internal):
- Baseline commit: 8x A100-eq covered under reserved rate.
- Large slab: priced at baseline * 2.7 / GPU-hour with 10% commit discount applied for 12-month deals.
- Expedited top-up premium: +20% per GPU-hour during cooldown.
- Hard cap option: must be set at onboarding; lifting the cap requires mission-critical approval and may trigger manual provisioning queues.

Grace — can you ask Nimbus whether they prefer soft-governor-with-premium or a hard block? If they want refunds for unused slabs we need to mark that as a one-off concession (impacts billing recognition). Rafael, fyi on cap/refund implications for revenue recognition.

—Marissa
Director, Customer Pricing | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Blake <sara@nimhealth.com>, Tom Lee <tom.lee@nimhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 08:02:33 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: top-up/throttle slab for autoscale & surge safety-net

Sara / Tom —

Appreciate the quick questions. Per Marissa's note, default is soft-governor-with-premium. That gives you the option to buy availability during cooldown windows for mission-critical batches. To make this concrete, we've attached an updated XLSX with three purchase paths:

A) Predictable spend path: slightly larger baseline commit + small monthly grace credits (lowest $ variance).
B) Flexible headroom path: medium baseline commit + large slabs + soft governor (best cost for high variance).
C) Conservative cap path: medium baseline commit + hard monthly top-up cap + ability to request one-off emergency bursts via a managed change (manual approval required).

I've attached a redlineable initial term sheet (redline-initial-draft.docx) and the updated pricing spreadsheet. If you prefer we can surface the "hard cap" as a checkbox on the SOW and default to soft-governor.

Tom — if procurement gives the green light on cap vs. soft approach, we can circulate the SOW and I can route for a 10% one-time onboarding credit (we typically reserve credits for 12-month commits).

Next actions: 1) Which path (A/B/C) does Nimbus prefer? 2) If C, procurement needs the SOW checkbox language — I can send that and Marissa will approve. 3) If B, we'll lock the slab sizing and finalize discounting.

Thanks,
Grace

Attachment: nim-topup-throttle-pricing-v1.xlsx (updated)
Attachment: redline-initial-draft.docx (term sheet)

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: top-up/throttle slab for autoscale & surge safety-net

Grace / team —

Thanks — Nimbus prefers path B (Flexible headroom) for production resiliency. Procurement is looping in our contracts lead and asked us to get a redlineable SOW and an explicit line that confirms the hard monthly spend cap option exists (even if we don't enable it immediately). They also requested that partial-hour consumption be pro-rated to the minute and that we receive the webhook for threshold alerts.

Can you send a redline-ready SOW and the final pricing spreadsheet with the 12-month commit discount applied? Once we have that, procurement will route internally and get back with any redlines (expect 3–5 business days).

Tom Lee
VP, Engineering | Nimbus Health
tom.lee@nimhealth.com | +1 (415) 555-3320
